passages.title: The Sugar Bush
passages.text: Every March, when the days turned warm but the nights still bit with frost, Grandpa Élie walked the maple trees behind his farmhouse with a hand drill. "The sap only runs when it thaws by day and freezes by night," he told Mireille, tapping a spile into the bark. She held the bucket steady while the first clear drops fell, slow as a leaking tap. It took forty litres of that watery sap to make just one litre of syrup, boiled for hours in the sugar shack until it thickened into gold. Mireille used to think maple syrup came from a bottle at the grocery store. Now, with sore arms and sap-sticky mittens, she understood why her grandfather called it liquid patience.

passages.title: The Last Streetlight
passages.text: Number seven was the only streetlight left standing on Larkin Avenue after the storm, and it flickered like it wasn't sure it should bother. Beneath it, three kids from the blackout block had dragged out lawn chairs, a deck of cards, and a flashlight for backup. "Lowest card loses a life," said Priya, dealing. Overhead, without the usual orange haze drowning them out, more stars showed than any of them had ever counted. Devon forgot to look at his hand entirely. "You can actually see the Milky Way," he said. Priya glanced up, then back down at her cards, unimpressed. "Play a card, or the Milky Way loses you your turn."

passages.title: The Monarch's Long Journey
passages.text: Each autumn, millions of monarch butterflies leave Canada and fly more than four thousand kilometres to the mountains of Mexico. No single butterfly makes the whole round trip. The ones that fly south are the great-grandchildren of the butterflies that left Mexico the previous spring, yet somehow they find the same forests their ancestors visited. Scientists believe they steer by the position of the sun and by an inner magnetic sense. In Mexico the monarchs cluster so thickly on the fir trees that the branches bend under their weight. There they rest through the winter, waiting for warm weather to begin the journey north again.

passages.title: The Substitute Goalie
passages.text: Nadia had never wanted to play goalie. She liked scoring, not stopping. But when Coach Bélanger's regular goalie broke a wrist the night before the semifinal, Nadia's hand went up before her brain could argue. The first period was a blur of flying pucks and banging pads. By the second, her knees stopped shaking. She stopped a hard slapshot with her glove, and the crowd roared so loudly that she almost forgot to be nervous. When the final buzzer sounded, the score was tied 2–2 and the game headed to a shootout. Nadia skated to the crease, tightened her mask, and took a deep breath. For once, she was exactly where she wanted to be.

questions.prompt: What is this passage mostly about?
choices: A grocery store that sells maple syrup
A girl learning how maple syrup is actually made
questions.explanation: The passage follows Mireille learning, through the tapping and boiling process, how much work goes into making maple syrup.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how much sap does it take to make one litre of syrup?
questions.explanation: The passage states it took forty litres of sap to make one litre of syrup.

questions.prompt: Why does Grandpa Élie call maple syrup "liquid patience"?
choices: Because it tastes better with age
Because making it takes a long, slow process
questions.explanation: The slow drip of sap and the hours of boiling described in the passage are what he means by "liquid patience".

questions.prompt: In the passage, the word "thaws" most nearly means:
questions.explanation: "Thaws by day and freezes by night" contrasts warming with freezing, so "thaws" means to melt or warm up.

questions.prompt: What is the author's main purpose in this passage?
choices: To argue that store-bought syrup is better
To tell a small story about a change in understanding
To compare Quebec and Ontario farms
questions.explanation: The passage is a short narrative about Mireille's understanding of syrup-making changing, not an argument or instructions.

questions.prompt: What game were the kids playing under the streetlight?
questions.explanation: Priya deals cards and says "lowest card loses a life," showing they are playing a card game.

questions.prompt: Why could the kids suddenly see so many stars?
choices: It was a clear night in the countryside
The power outage removed the streetlights' glow
questions.explanation: The passage notes the usual "orange haze" from streetlights was gone, letting more stars show — a result of the blackout.

questions.prompt: How does Priya's reaction to the stars compare with Devon's?
choices: She is just as amazed as he is
She is more focused on the game than the sky
She has never seen stars before
She is afraid of the dark
questions.explanation: While Devon is awestruck, Priya glances up briefly and returns her attention to the card game, showing she is more focused on playing.

questions.prompt: In the passage, "unimpressed" most nearly means:
questions.explanation: Priya's quick glance and return to the game shows she was not particularly interested — unimpressed.

questions.prompt: What happened right after the storm, according to the passage?
choices: The kids went inside to sleep
Number seven was the only streetlight left standing
The power came back on immediately
questions.explanation: The passage opens by stating number seven was the only streetlight left standing on Larkin Avenue after the storm.

questions.prompt: Which word in this sentence is an adjective? "The enormous whale surfaced quietly."
questions.explanation: "Enormous" describes the noun "whale," making it an adjective.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "Neither of the boys ___ ready."
questions.explanation: "Neither" is singular, so it takes the singular verb "is."

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the past perfect tense correctly?
choices: She had finished her homework before dinner.
She finish her homework before dinner.
She finishing her homework before dinner.
She will finished her homework before dinner.
questions.explanation: Past perfect uses "had" + past participle to show an action completed before another past action: "had finished."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: "Give the book to Marc and ___."
questions.explanation: As the object of the preposition "to," the correct pronoun is "me," not "I."

questions.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: Its a beautiful day, isn't it?
It's a beautiful day, isn't it?
Its' a beautiful day, isnt it?
It's a beautiful day, isnt it?
questions.explanation: "It's" is the contraction for "it is," and the tag question needs an apostrophe: "isn't."

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: "___ going to the park after school."
questions.explanation: "They're" is the contraction for "they are," which fits here.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: "Please put the books over ___."
questions.explanation: "There" refers to a place, which fits this sentence.

questions.prompt: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: The correct spelling follows "i before e except after c": receive.

questions.prompt: In the sentence "She quickly closed the door," what part of speech is "quickly"?
questions.explanation: "Quickly" describes how she closed the door, making it an adverb.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the future tense?
questions.explanation: "Will walk" indicates an action that has not happened yet — the future tense.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses commas correctly?
choices: I packed pencils pens and a ruler.
I packed pencils, pens, and a ruler.
I packed, pencils pens and a ruler.
I packed pencils pens, and a ruler.
questions.explanation: Items in a series are separated by commas, including before "and" in the Oxford comma style: pencils, pens, and a ruler.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "One of the scientists ___ presenting tomorrow."
questions.explanation: The subject is "One," which is singular, so it takes the singular verb "is." ("Of the scientists" only tells us which one.)

questions.prompt: Which word means the same as "enormous"?
questions.explanation: "Huge" is a synonym for "enormous" — both mean very large.

questions.prompt: Which word is the opposite of "generous"?
questions.explanation: "Stingy" means unwilling to give, the opposite of "generous."

questions.prompt: Puppy is to dog as kitten is to ___.
questions.explanation: A puppy is a baby dog, just as a kitten is a baby cat.

questions.prompt: "The classroom was a zoo" is an example of a:
questions.explanation: A metaphor directly states one thing is another (without "like" or "as"), comparing the classroom to a zoo.

questions.prompt: "Her smile was as bright as the sun" is an example of a:
questions.explanation: A simile compares two things using "like" or "as" — here, "as bright as the sun."

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses personification?
choices: The wind howled through the trees.
questions.explanation: Giving the wind a human ability — "howled" — is personification.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom "it's raining cats and dogs" mean?
choices: Animals are falling from the sky
questions.explanation: This idiom simply means it is raining very hard — it isn't literal.

questions.prompt: Which word means the same as "reluctant"?
questions.explanation: "Reluctant" and "unwilling" both describe hesitation to do something.

questions.prompt: Which word is the opposite of "ancient"?
questions.explanation: "Modern" is the opposite of "ancient," which means very old.

questions.prompt: Author is to book as composer is to ___.
questions.explanation: Just as an author writes a book, a composer writes a song (or piece of music).

questions.prompt: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Trout, salmon, and cod are all fish; a dolphin is a mammal.

questions.prompt: What letter comes next? B, D, F, H, ___
questions.explanation: The pattern skips one letter each time (B, D, F, H), so the next letter is J.

questions.prompt: If CAT is coded as DBU, how is DOG coded using the same rule?
questions.explanation: Each letter shifts forward by one in the alphabet: D→E, O→P, G→H, giving EPH.

questions.prompt: Hot is to cold as up is to ___.
questions.explanation: "Hot" and "cold" are opposites, just as "up" and "down" are opposites.

questions.prompt: Facing north, you turn 90 degrees to your right. Which direction are you facing now?
questions.explanation: Turning 90 degrees right (clockwise) from north points you east.

questions.prompt: Which word does not belong with the others?
questions.explanation: Triangle, square, and circle are 2D shapes; a cube is a 3D shape.

questions.prompt: What comes next? Z, X, V, T, ___
questions.explanation: The pattern moves backward, skipping one letter each time (Z, X, V, T), so the next letter is R.

questions.prompt: You walk 3 blocks north, then 2 blocks east, then 3 blocks south. Which direction must you walk to return to your starting point?
questions.explanation: The north and south walks cancel out, leaving you 2 blocks east of the start, so you must walk west to return.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of this passage?
choices: Monarch butterflies make a remarkable long-distance migration
Butterflies are the most colourful insects in Canada
Fir trees in Mexico are slowly dying
Scientists are building tools that copy butterfly wings
questions.explanation: The whole passage describes how monarchs travel from Canada to Mexico and back again.

questions.prompt: About how far do monarchs fly to reach Mexico?
questions.explanation: The first sentence says they fly more than four thousand kilometres.

questions.prompt: What can you conclude about the butterflies that fly south in the autumn?
choices: They have made the trip several times
They learned the route from scientists
They have never been to Mexico before
They are the same butterflies that left Mexico in the spring
questions.explanation: They are the great-grandchildren of the butterflies that left Mexico, so they are making the trip for the first time.

questions.prompt: In the passage, the word "cluster" most nearly means
questions.explanation: The monarchs cover the fir trees so thickly that the branches bend, so "cluster" means to gather in a tight group.

questions.prompt: Why did the author most likely write this passage?
choices: To inform readers about how monarchs migrate
To persuade readers to plant fir trees
To tell a funny story about one butterfly
To warn readers about dangerous insects
questions.explanation: The passage explains facts about the monarch migration, so its purpose is to inform.

questions.prompt: How does Nadia most likely feel at the start of the game?
questions.explanation: Her knees are shaking and she is nervous, which shows she is unsure at first.

questions.prompt: Which event happens first?
choices: Nadia stops a slapshot with her glove
The game goes to a shootout
The regular goalie breaks a wrist
questions.explanation: The goalie is hurt the night before the semifinal, before any of the game events.

questions.prompt: What was the score when the final buzzer sounded?
questions.explanation: The passage says the score was tied 2–2 and the game headed to a shootout.

questions.prompt: What does the last sentence suggest about Nadia?
choices: She has become comfortable and confident as a goalie
She still wishes she were scoring goals
She is planning to quit hockey
She is afraid of the shootout
questions.explanation: "Exactly where she wanted to be" shows she now feels at home in the net.

questions.prompt: In the passage, the word "blur" most nearly means
choices: something that happens too fast to see clearly
questions.explanation: Flying pucks and banging pads describe a first period that went by too quickly to follow.

questions.prompt: Which word is an adverb in this sentence? "The children quietly entered the library."
questions.explanation: "Quietly" tells how the children entered, so it is an adverb.

questions.prompt: Which word is a preposition in this sentence? "The cat slept under the warm blanket."
questions.explanation: "Under" shows where the cat slept in relation to the blanket, so it is a preposition.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: Each of the students ___ a backpack.
questions.explanation: "Each" is singular, so it takes the singular verb "has".

questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
choices: The books on the shelf is dusty.
The books on the shelf are dusty.
The book on the shelves are dusty.
The books on the shelf was dusty.
questions.explanation: The subject is "books" (plural), so the verb must be "are".

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the past tense correctly?
choices: Yesterday, she runs to the bus stop.
Yesterday, she runned to the bus stop.
Yesterday, she ran to the bus stop.
Yesterday, she will run to the bus stop.
questions.explanation: The past tense of "run" is "ran". "Runned" is not a word.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: By the time we arrived, the movie ___ already started.
questions.explanation: "Had" shows the movie started before we arrived (past perfect).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct pronoun: Maya and ___ went to the museum.
questions.explanation: Take out "Maya and": "___ went to the museum" needs the subject pronoun "I".

questions.prompt: Which word correctly completes the sentence? The dog wagged ___ tail happily.
questions.explanation: "Its" shows possession. "It's" means "it is" or "it has".

questions.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: Before we leave please, turn off the lights.
Before we leave, please turn off, the lights.
Before we leave, please turn off the lights.
Before, we leave please turn off the lights.
questions.explanation: A comma goes after the introductory phrase "Before we leave".

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses apostrophes correctly?
questions.explanation: "Can't" needs an apostrophe where the letters are missing, and "Sam's" shows the jacket belongs to Sam.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct word: I have ___ much homework to finish tonight.
questions.explanation: "Too" means "more than needed" or "very". "To" is a preposition and "two" is the number.

questions.prompt: Which word is spelled correctly?
questions.explanation: "Necessary" has one c and two s: one collar, two sleeves.

questions.prompt: Which word means the same as "enormous"?
questions.explanation: "Enormous" means very large, just like "huge".

questions.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to "reluctant"?
questions.explanation: A reluctant person does not want to do something, so "unwilling" is closest.

questions.prompt: Which word is the opposite of "ancient"?
questions.explanation: "Ancient" means very old, and "modern" means new or recent.

questions.prompt: Which word is the opposite of "generous"?
questions.explanation: A generous person gives freely; a selfish person keeps things for themselves.

questions.prompt: Bird is to nest as bee is to ___.
questions.explanation: A nest is where a bird lives, and a hive is where a bee lives.

questions.prompt: Author is to book as painter is to ___.
questions.explanation: An author creates a book, and a painter creates a painting.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is a metaphor?
choices: The classroom was a zoo during the storm.
The classroom was as loud as a zoo.
The classroom was like a zoo.
questions.explanation: A metaphor says one thing IS another without using "like" or "as".

questions.prompt: What kind of figurative language is this? "Her smile was as bright as the sun."
questions.explanation: It compares two things using "as", which makes it a simile.

questions.prompt: Which sentence uses personification?
choices: The wind blew hard through the trees.
The wind was as cold as ice.
The wind whispered secrets through the trees.
The trees were tall and green.
questions.explanation: Whispering secrets is something people do, so the wind is given a human action.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom "break the ice" mean?
choices: To cause damage to a frozen lake
To start a conversation in an awkward situation
questions.explanation: To break the ice means to make people feel more relaxed, often by starting a friendly conversation.

questions.prompt: Which word does not belong with the others: apple, banana, carrot, grape?
questions.explanation: Apple, banana and grape are fruits. A carrot is a vegetable.

questions.prompt: Which word does not belong with the others: triangle, square, circle, cube?
questions.explanation: Triangle, square and circle are flat shapes. A cube is a solid shape.

questions.prompt: What comes next in the series? A, C, E, G, ___
questions.explanation: The series skips one letter each time: A, (B), C, (D), E, (F), G, (H), I.

questions.prompt: What comes next in the series? Z, X, V, T, ___
questions.explanation: The letters go backward, skipping one each time: Z, (Y), X, (W), V, (U), T, (S), R.

questions.prompt: In a code, CAT is written as DBU (each letter moves one place forward in the alphabet). How is DOG written in this code?
questions.explanation: D→E, O→P, G→H, so DOG becomes EPH.

questions.prompt: Which pair has the same relationship as "pencil : write"?
questions.explanation: A pencil is used to write, and scissors are used to cut.

questions.prompt: Sam faces north. He turns right, then turns right again. Which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation: Turning right from north points east, and turning right again points south.

questions.prompt: Ava walks 3 blocks east, then 3 blocks north, then 3 blocks west. Where is she compared with where she started?
questions.explanation: The east and west walks cancel out, leaving her 3 blocks north.
